claims.text:
stage computation: Inputs are all four pairs (x0,x1)∈{−1,+1}². Frozen representation phi(x)=x0. For target y=x0 fit scalar least-squares head w=sum(phi*y)/sum(phi²)=1; predictions match all four, SSE0. Change new-task target to y=x1: same frozen representation gives w0 and SSE4. No head can distinguish opposite labels at an identical code.

**Countercase / boundary:** Allow a richer frozen representation phi=(x0,x1) and fit the linear head [0,1] for y=x1: SSE0. Successful transfer depends on retained information and target, not merely freezing weights; these finite exact fits establish no real data-efficiency claim.

**Prediction / transfer recall:** Predict whether a head can recover x1 from x0 alone on these four examples; recall two inputs with same code and conflicting targets rule out perfect deterministic prediction from that code.

**Intervention / reachable witness:** Fit head, Change task, Restore feature controls compute code/target/prediction table and SSE, keeping original fit and conflicting-code witness. Frozen encoder and trainable head must be visibly separate.
